comment: Each listed verdict compares the exact byte-pinned source-anchor bundle and explicitly pinned semantic context with Lean's fully expanded paper-local semantic target and Lean-elaborated parameter, premise, and conclusion roles. The paired proof endpoint is reviewed separately.

NoothigattuEtAl2020PairwiseComparisons.c.reason: Source item claimA_1 at cited publication:780-784 states that for positive real h and t, the displayed coin-flip log-likelihood is strictly concave on p in (0,1) and has its unique maximum at h/(h+t). The expanded Lean target has exactly the two positivity assumptions, StrictConcaveOn on Set.Ioo 0 1, membership and IsMaxOn at heads/(heads+tails), and equality of every other in-domain maximizer to that point, so its scope and conclusion coincide with the source item.

Source item claimC_1 at cited publication:1055-1055 quantifies positive real c,d,e,f, assumes c>d and e>f, and concludes ce+df>cf+de. The expanded Lean target quantifies the same four reals, lists the same six positivity/order assumptions as 0<c, 0<d, 0<e, 0<f, d<c, f<e, and has the identical strict crossed-product conclusion.

NoothigattuEtAl2020PairwiseComparisons.l.reason: Source item lemma2_1 at cited publication:207-216 states, in the included finite-alternative, CDF-like-link, fixed-reference MLE context, that for continuous strictly monotone F an MLE exists iff every undirected comparison component is directed strongly connected. The expanded Lean target quantifies a finite Alternative type, dataset, CDF-like link, and reference, assumes Continuous and StrictMono, and asserts exactly the equivalence between existence of a reference-normalized pairwise MLE score and everyComponentStronglyConnected.

Source item lemma2_2 at cited publication:217-223 assumes continuous strictly monotone F, that a has exactly one comparison neighbor b, and positive counts in both directions, and says every MLE has score difference equal to the perfect-fit inverse value. The expanded Lean target has the same MLE, one-neighbor, two-positive-count, continuity, and strict-monotonicity premises and asserts a unique delta with F(delta) equal to the observed win fraction and score(first)-score(second)=delta; under the stated strict monotonicity this is precisely the source's F-inverse formulation.

Source item lemma2_3 at cited publication:224-227 gives, for positive counts in both directions on every pair in X^2 and continuous strictly monotone F, the bound ||score||_infinity <= |X| times the maximum perfect-fit distance. The queue's model context defines X^2 as distinct ordered pairs, and the expanded Lean target accordingly assumes positive count for every distinct ordered pair, quantifies every MLE, uses scoreSupNorm, and concludes the same card(Alternative) times maxPerfectFitDistance bound with the same continuity and strict-monotonicity hypotheses.

Source item lemma2_4 at cited publication:239-240 says that under strict log-concavity, likelihood strict concavity together with uniqueness of any existing MLE holds iff the comparison graph is connected. The expanded Lean target assumes StrictConcaveOn of log F, places likelihood strict concavity on the fixed-reference score domain from the source model, expresses 'unique assuming it exists' as equality of any two MLEs without adding existence, and makes exactly that conjunction equivalent to dataset.isConnected.

NoothigattuEtAl2020PairwiseComparisons.t.reason: Source item theorem3_2 at cited publication:266-271 says that for a strictly monotone CDF-like F, maximum likelihood estimation satisfies Definition 3.1. The expanded theorem target universally fixes the CDF-like link, assumes exactly StrictMono link.toFun, and concludes the graph-bound definition3_1_pareto_efficiency for that same link. Its supporting declaration quantifies every finite dataset, fixed-reference MLE score, and alternative pair and, under the exact source count conditions (strict direct majority plus strictly better outgoing and incoming counts against every other alternative), concludes score(second) <= score(first), matching Definition 3.1 and the source proof synopsis that rules out score(first) < score(second).

Source item theorem4_2 at cited publication:324-371 says that MLE for a strictly monotone, log-concave, differentiable CDF-like F satisfies Definition 4.1. The expanded theorem target has exactly StrictMono link.toFun, non-strict ConcaveOn of log(link.toFun), and Differentiable link.toFun, then concludes the graph-bound definition4_1_monotonicitySpec for the same fixed link. That supporting property quantifies finite alternatives and expands through pairwiseMLEMonotonicity: the updated dataset changes only the directed winner-loser count and increases it strictly, both datasets have unique fixed-reference MLEs, and their MLE scores satisfy the source's weak winner-up and loser-down difference inequalities relative to every alternative. Thus the dependency and theorem preserve the full source scope without adding uniqueness as an external theorem hypothesis.

Theorem 5.3 states that maximum-likelihood estimation violates pairwise majority consistency whenever the source link F is strictly monotonic, strictly log-concave, and differentiable. The expanded Lean target universally quantifies a CDFLikePairwiseLink, assumes StrictMono for F, StrictConcaveOn all real gaps for log composed with F, and differentiability of F, then concludes the negation of definition5_1_pairwise_majority_consistencySpec. The displayed link structure supplies the governing random-utility CDF conditions. The displayed Definition 5.1 closure universally quantifies finite alternatives, datasets, reference-normalized MLE scores, and complete labelings with strict direct-count majorities, and requires the corresponding weak score order. Its negation therefore says exactly that this MLE rule has a counterexample to PMC under the theorem's link conditions. Reference normalization only fixes the additive score representative and does not change majority or score ordering. No source premise, quantifier, or conclusion is added, omitted, or narrowed.

Source item theorem6_3 at cited publication:485-496 says that every strictly monotone, strictly log-concave, differentiable CDF-like F yields an MLE-rule violation of Definition 6.1 separability. The expanded theorem target universally fixes that link, assumes exactly StrictMono link.toFun, StrictConcaveOn of log(link.toFun), and Differentiable link.toFun, and negates the graph-bound definition6_1_separabilitySpec for the same link. The supporting property expands through pairwiseMLESeparable to two datasets and their MLEs under that link, assumes both strictly rank the same pair, pointwise-pools their counts, and requires every pooled-data MLE to preserve the strict ordering. This is precisely the source definition, so its negation matches the stated theorem violation.
